- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after a recent spike (e.g., >70) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 3–7 days post-spike.
- Model overestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral — reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 1–2%.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct — add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment for next 3–5 days.
- Forecast horizon 1–7 days: model often lags sentiment shifts — align forecast with sentiment direction within 1–2 days.
- Forecast horizon 8–30 days: model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment — dampen forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment is volatile or recent.
